title: DA: California mistress charged as accessory after man is accused of killing wife, mother-in-law - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago MARTINEZ, Calif. – The Contra Costa District Attorney’s Office has filed felony and misdemeanor charges against an Oakland woman in connection with the September 18 murders of two women in Walnut Creek.
Photo by JOSHUA COLEMAN on Unsplash Prosecutors announced that 45-year-old Yan Wang has been charged as an accessory after the fact in the killings of Linlin Guo and her mother, Beimin Cheng. Wang is scheduled to be arraigned on September 30 at 1:30 p.m. in Contra Costa Superior Court in Martinez.
Howard Wang, who was married to Guo and in a romantic relationship with Yan Wang at the time of the murders, was charged on September 22 with the unlawful killing of both women. He is scheduled to be arraigned in Martinez on October 3. If convicted, he faces life in prison without the possibility of parole.
Yan Wang, who has no familial relation to Howard Wang, faces three charges. She is accused of violating PC 32, felony accessory after the fact, for allegedly helping Howard Wang avoid arrest, trial, conviction, and punishment. She also faces PC 459, felony first-degree residential burglary, for allegedly entering the Walnut Creek residence shared by Howard Wang and Linlin Guo with intent to commit larceny on or about September 19. Additionally, she faces PC 135, misdemeanor destroying evidence, for allegedly destroying cellphones on September 18.
“This case serves as a sobering reminder of domestic violence’s far-reaching consequences,” said Contra Costa District Attorney Diana Becton. “Our office will pursue justice with the seriousness and urgency this tragedy demands.”
The case, The People of the State of California v. Yan Wang (No. 01-25-03240), continues in Contra Costa County Superior Court.
